- **Boundary:** Paste text: channel `send.text`, MCP `send.text`, CLI `send` stdin/`--file`
  - **What to validate:** **Rule (exact set):** multi-line text is normal (relays, plans and free-text answers are multi-line, brief §4.1 S1), so three controls are **allowed**: LF (U+000A), CR (U+000D) and TAB (U+0009). Everything else in this set is **refused**: every other C0 control (U+0000–U+0008, U+000B–U+000C, U+000E–U+001F, including ESC U+001B above all), DEL (U+007F) and every C1 control (U+0080–U+009F, including CSI U+009B). The check runs over decoded `char`s of the UTF-8 `&str`, never over raw bytes, because UTF-8 continuation bytes 0x80–0xBF are not C1 controls. This stops a bracketed-paste breakout through an embedded `ESC[201~`. **Reject, don't strip:** a text that holds a refused character is refused whole; no refused character is ever removed and the rest typed. **The typed text, an inner CR as one LF and the trailing CR and LF removed, allowed characters only:** after `validate_paste_text` has passed on the text as received, the wrapper's `send` takes the typed text once (`viola_agent_claude::hook::typed_text`: every CR LF pair as one LF, every other CR as one LF, and every trailing CR and LF removed, in any order; it holds no CR, and nothing else changes, not a TAB, a space, or an LF that is not at the very end), and from there on it is the only text `send` uses: the local-command classification (a listed local command followed by LF, CR or CRLF is that command: `/clear` and a CRLF is `/clear`), the in-flight text the delivery-confirmation exact match compares, `text_bytes` and the paste. A text that ends in CR, LF or CRLF and holds a refused character is still refused `control-character` with nothing typed.
 The LF removal is the founder's ruling, live, 2026-10-07T15:21Z, every option and the `/clear`-plus-newline consequence shown to him, relayed by the overseer (chunk 2026-10-07-a-send-ending-in-a-newline-is-confirmed); the CR and CRLF removal is the founder's ruling, live, 2026-10-09, the options shown, relayed by the overseer (chunk 2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup); typing a CR or a CR LF inside a text as the LF the CLI submits is the founder's ruling, live in the overseer's dialog, 2026-10-09T16:51Z, the options shown, relayed by the operator (chunk 2026-10-09-inner-cr-and-crlf-in-a-sent-text). Only CR and LF, both allowed characters, are rewritten or removed: the set of accepted texts is unchanged, the typed text of a valid text is valid and holds no character that is neither in the received text nor LF (a 512-case property pins it), no refused character is typed or removed, a raw channel client gets the same rule from the wrapper, and the delivery-confirmation match stays an exact equality with no tolerance on the submitted side. **An empty typed text is refused:** a text whose typed text is empty, the empty text included, is refused `not-delivered` / `empty-text` (`NotDelivered::EmptyText`, exit 13) on both sides: by the client (`refusal_of` in `src/cmd/send.rs`, which reads a refused character first and then the empty typed text) before any frame, with a `send-refused{side:"client"}` line, and by the wrapper's `send` directly after the typed text is taken and before the first wheel read, with nothing reserved, issued or typed (the name, the condition and the hint are the founder's ruling of 2026-10-09, relayed; the rung is the overseer's).
 **Where it runs:** `viola_core::validate_paste_text(&str) -> Result<(), NotDelivered>` (`Err(NotDelivered::ControlCharacter)`), called client-side before sending (CLI `viola send` in `src/cmd/send.rs`: exit 13 before any frame and a `send-refused{side:"client"}` line; the MCP `send` tool in `viola-mcp`, since chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers: `validate_paste_text`, then the empty-typed-text check, each refused as `{"refusal":"not-delivered","detail":"control-character"|"empty-text"}` with one client-side `send-refused` line, before any frame) and again by the wrapper's `send` (`src/run/send.rs`) before anything is typed — first in its refusal order, and authoritative. The paste itself is one `ESC[200~…ESC[201~` + CR `write_all` of the typed text through `viola-pty`'s `PasteHandle`. **Wire outcome:** refusal `not-delivered` with detail `control-character`, then `not-delivered` with detail `empty-text`, both checked before the Conventions refusal order.
  - **How (stack-specific):** `viola-core`; `src/cmd/send.rs`; `src/run/send.rs`; `viola-pty` `PasteHandle`

- **Boundary:** Hook stdin (all hook events + `hook statusline`)
  - **What to validate:** **Size cap:** `Read::take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` on `read_to_end`, so an over-limit payload is detected, never silently truncated; over the limit, fail open (exit 0, no body, `hook-decision` detail `oversize-stdin` + `parse-rejected{parser:"hook-stdin", detail:"oversize"}` in `diagnostics/`). **Event argument:** the word `statusline` (with no `--capture`) is taken first and is not a `HookEvent`; any other `<event>` maps into the closed `HookEvent` (9 events: the seven spine and async events plus the dialog tier, `PreToolUse` and `PermissionRequest`); an unknown event, a clap error or an absent/invalid `VIOLA_NAME` exits 0 with nothing written anywhere. **One object:** a payload that is not one JSON object fails open with `malformed-json`. **Parsing:** tolerant (Established Decisions: Validation), but fields that decide security (dialog kind and the decision body) map into closed enums in `viola-agent-claude`: on the dialog path `viola_agent_claude::dialog::classify` maps the one object into `DialogKind` / `DialogTool`, a malformed dialog payload fails open (`AgentError::DialogMalformed`: exit 0, no body), the reply read is bounded at `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX + 5 s` (3605 s: the ceiling, the wrapper replying `null` at its own configured hold's end), and stdout takes one write. **Question and Stop data:** each question's `option_details` takes an option's `description` and `preview` only as strings, else `null`, and never refuses the dialog (`options` keeps its labels); the Stop's `background_tasks` is read as an array of `serde::de::IgnoredAny` and carried only as its length, no element read, `null` when absent, `null` or not an array (a non-array also writes the drift entry `{"path":"background_tasks","expected":"array"}`).
 The option text crossing into `events.ndjson`, `hook.dialog`, CLI `wait --json` and the MCP `wait` is a boundary widening the founder answered himself (P4 fork Q4 of chunk 2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola, relayed by the overseer), and `background_tasks` is a count only by the same answer. **Statusline payload (`hook statusline`):** the same cap and the same one-object rule, each ending in exit 0, empty stderr, nothing printed and no `budget.json`. `viola_agent_claude::statusline::reading` is tolerant on every field: no `rate_limits` object is no reading and no write; a window that is absent or not an object is the word `"unknown"`; `used_percentage` is kept only from 0 to 100, else `"unknown"`; `resets_at` is epoch seconds or RFC 3339, written as RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds, and a malformed value becomes `"unknown"`. `budget.json` is written only by this arm. **Capture arm (hidden, `hook <event> --capture <DIR> [--answers <DIR>]`, called only by `viola verify`'s probe plugins):** `<DIR>` must be absolute and exist; stdin is read through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` and written raw (verify parses it later) to an exclusively claimed `<DIR>/<PascalEvent>.<k>.json`: `viola_state::fs::create_private_new` creates it new at 0600 from `free_k`'s first free `k`, the next `k` on `AlreadyExists`, then `replace_private` writes over its own claim, so two concurrent captures never share a name. `--answers <DIR>` is read only with `--capture` (inert without it): for a dialog event (PreToolUse / PermissionRequest), the event's ordinal `j` in claim order selects `<DIR>/<Event>.<j>`, read through `take(64)` and matched exactly against the closed `ProbeAnswer` ids; `ledger::probe_body` shape-checks the filed payload (`None` on a miss) and builds the body only through `dialog::decision_body`; stdout takes one write.
 It reads no `VIOLA_*`, does no obs init and opens no channel; any failure prints and writes nothing; stderr is always empty and the exit always 0. A boundary widening ratified live by the founder at 2026-09-28 20:24:32 (Decisions Log `2026-09-28`, capture arm); the `--answers` body is the founder's live ruling of 2026-10-05 (M7 = A, the hook answers, never a key), relayed by the overseer. **Statusline capture arm (hidden, `hook statusline --capture <DIR> [--shell <WORD>]`, called only by Run B's probe settings):** taken before the statusline pass-through; `<DIR>` must be absolute and exist; stdin through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`, refused past `MAX_FRAME`; the payload is written raw at the first free `StatusLine.<k>.json` through the same `create_private_new` claim and `replace_private` 0600 write, and `StatusLine.<k>.shell` holds exactly `bin-sh` when the `--shell` word equals `/bin/sh` byte for byte, else `other` (a missing word is `other`, the closed `ShellVerdict`); the word itself is written nowhere. It prints nothing, exits 0 on every path, reads no `VIOLA_*`, does no obs init and opens no channel, `budget.json` or snapshot; `--shell` on any other arm changes nothing, and `hook statusline` without `--capture` is unchanged. `viola verify` reads the files back through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` (the shell file capped at 16 bytes) into `ShellVerdict`. The founder's own answer to P4 fork 3 of chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows («Run B + --settings», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I1`).
  - **How (stack-specific):** `viola-agent-claude` hook parser, `statusline::reading` and `ledger::probe_body`; root `src/cmd/hook.rs` `capture` / `free_k` / `file_from` and `src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs`; `viola_state::fs::create_private_new`; serde_path_to_error 0.1.20; chrono 0.4.45

- **Boundary:** CLI arguments / stdin
  - **What to validate:** **Names:** every `ViolaName` argument uses `#[arg(value_parser = parse_viola_name)]`, which calls `ViolaName::try_new`. **Home path:** `--home` and `VIOLA_DIR` are canonicalised (`std::fs::canonicalize`, once the home exists; the plain drive form on Windows — the resolution as landed is **Home resolution** below) and then pass the `~/.viola/` strict-modes check before any snapshot, `statusline_command` or ledger read. Interim gaps (ratified, until the Epoch 6 entry "Home and code-bearing file integrity"): `viola hook <event>`, on its nine `HookEvent` arms, does not canonicalise `VIOLA_DIR` or run the strict-modes check (`hook statusline` is outside this gap: it canonicalises its instance directory and runs `viola_state::strict::check_instance` before its log opens and before any stdin, `budget.json`, snapshot or `statusline_command` use); on its event path it requires an absolute `VIOLA_DIR` ending `<home>/instances/<name>` and a `VIOLA_NAME` that passes `ViolaName::try_new`, and is otherwise a silent no-op (Decisions Log `2026-09-28`); its hidden `--capture <DIR>` arm (and `hook statusline --capture <DIR>`, whose hidden `--shell <WORD>` maps only into the closed `ShellVerdict`) reads no `VIOLA_*` and requires an absolute, existing `<DIR>` instead, and its hidden `--answers <DIR>` is read only with `--capture`, each answer file through `take(64)` into the closed `ProbeAnswer` id (Hook stdin row). `viola verify` reads `ledger/stamps.json` before any strict-modes check (Decisions Log `2026-09-28`, stamps read); `viola run`'s version gate reads it through `read_stamps_strict`. **`answer` response:** the JSON from stdin or `--file` is read with `Read::take(MAX_FRAME)` into the closed `response` enums.
 **`send` text:** from stdin or `--file` only, read with `Read::take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`; over the cap or not UTF-8 is exit 2 with one fixed line, a second positional argument is a clap usage error, and the text then passes `validate_paste_text` and the empty-typed-text check (`refusal_of`: `not-delivered` / `control-character`, then `not-delivered` / `empty-text`; exit 13), both before any frame. A fourth interim gap (the founder's ruling, live, 2026-10-04, relayed by the overseer), owed to the Epoch 6 entry "Home and code-bearing file integrity": `viola send` reads `snapshot.json` without the strict-modes check, resolves the endpoint, `pid` and `started_at` through the liveness pre-check `live_endpoint`, and then, on Linux and Windows, verifies the serving process against them before the frame (IPC client-side server verification row). A fifth interim gap (the same founder's ruling, live, 2026-10-04, relayed by the overseer), owed to the same entry: `viola wait` and `viola last` read `snapshot.json` the same way. A sixth (the founder's ruling F1, live, 2026-10-04, relayed by the overseer), owed to the same entry: `viola answer` reads it the same way. A seventh (the founder's ruling F-W1, live, 2026-10-04, relayed by the overseer), owed to the same entry: `viola pause` and `viola release` read it the same way. An eighth (the founder's own answer to P4 fork Q1, live, 2026-10-17, relayed by the overseer, `inputs#I2` of chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers), owed to the same entry: `viola mcp`'s `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` tools read it the same way (`viola_state::liveness::live_endpoint`). **`wait` / `last` arguments:** `<name>` through `ViolaName::try_new` (the verbs share `send`'s name parser), and `--after` / `--timeout-ms` are clap `u64` (a non-integer is a usage error, exit 2). **`answer` arguments:** `<name>` through `ViolaName::try_new`, `<dialog_id>` a clap `u64`.
 **`pause` / `release` arguments:** `<name>` through `ViolaName::try_new`; their `from` comes from `VIOLA_NAME` only. **`revive` arguments:** `<name>` through `ViolaName::try_new` (the verbs' shared name parser); `--id <ID>` through a clap value parser that accepts only the session-id shape (anything else is a usage error, exit 2); `--list` conflicts with `--id`, `--fork` and the trailing arguments; the words after `--` go to the child as argv elements of a direct spawn; `--json` is accepted on both arms (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract): a refused strict-modes check or a preflight refusal then prints exactly `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` on stdout (stderr empty, exit 1), `<code>` one of the closed `strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing` (through `client::refused_document`), and `--list --json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{"sessions":[{"ts","cause","id"},…]}}` in log order (the escaped `ts`, the closed cause word, the session-shaped id) — codes, closed words and session-shaped ids only, never a path or pid; a refusal `run`'s start makes after a passed preflight prints no document (owed to the route entry "Exit-cause code catalogue"); `--list` under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME` logs `process-start` / `process-exit` in the caller's `cli-<VIOLA_NAME>.ndjson` only after its strict-modes check passed. Both arms run the strict-modes check on the instance's files before any snapshot or log value is used, so `viola revive` is not among this row's interim gaps. **`list` arguments:** `[--json]` only, no name.
 **`link` / `unlink` arguments:** `<driver>` and `<driven>` through `ViolaName::try_new` (the verbs' shared name parser), and `--json`; the verbs' instance is the driven one, `instances/<driven>` joined only from that parsed name and checked by `check_instance` before any snapshot read, so neither verb is among this row's interim gaps. A `driver` equal to `driven` is not refused client-side: the wrapper refuses it (`-32602`, the Channel frames row).

The CLI verbs' `VIOLA_DIR` step and the canonicalisation, `mcp`'s use of them included, widen what chooses a CLI verb's home: a widening the founder ratified (his own word, relayed verbatim by the operator, 2026-10-19). `viola list`'s `board::scan` then runs `check_path` on the home and on `instances/` (each through `symlink_metadata`, a link never followed) and `check_instance` per instance before any file under the home is opened (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list).
  - **How (stack-specific):** `src/main.rs` clap 4.6.7 derive; `viola-state` home resolution

- **Boundary:** Configuration values (`config.json`)
  - **What to validate:** Tolerant parse (unknown keys counted). The budget thresholds are the two top-level keys `five_hour` and `seven_day` (defaults 90 and 85), read once at the wrapper's start, and by `viola list` at each run, both through `run::budget::read_thresholds` under the same rule (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list; each rejection is logged through `obs::log_config_rejection`, under a `VIOLA_NAME` only, and a refused `list` reads no `config.json`): a value must be a JSON whole number that fits `Percent` (0–100, `Percent::try_new`), else that key alone takes its default and is reported as one `parse-rejected{parser:"config-json", detail:"malformed"}` line per bad key; a document that is no object, or whose `v` is not 1, gives both defaults and no rejection from this read; no value of either key switches the gate off. The dialog hold is the top-level key `dialog_hold_s`, read once at the wrapper's start through `run::dialog::read_hold` right after the thresholds: a JSON whole number of seconds that fits `DialogHold` (60–3600, `DialogHold::try_new`; default 60, `DIALOG_HOLD_DEFAULT`), else the hold takes 60 and is reported as one `parse-rejected{parser:"config-json", detail:"malformed"}` line; a document that is no object, or whose `v` is not 1, gives 60 and no rejection from this read; no value makes the hold zero or unbounded, and no env var or flag sets it (a boundary widening the founder answered himself, chunk 2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver, `inputs#I2` Q1). `port` goes into `u16`. `diagnostics_level` is the closed set `info` \| `debug`; any other value falls back to `info` and is reported as `parse-rejected`. `claude_env_keep` (the Unix R8 pass-list) is an array of at most 32 names, each matching `^CLAUDE[A-Z0-9_]*$`; a bad value is rejected WHOLE (never partly accepted) and reported as `parse-rejected`, and an identity-floor name in it has no effect (not an error). `v` is checked, and the read is capped at `MAX_FRAME`.

  - **What to validate:** **Line cap:** replay and tail read each ndjson line with a `MAX_FRAME` cap; an over-long line counts as `torn_lines`. As landed, the one `events.ndjson` reader (`viola_state::events::read_from`: the wrapper's `wait` scan and `last` rebuild, `viola_state::replay::session_chain`, the one pass `viola revive` reads the logged session ids from, and since chunk 2026-10-10-session-links the wrapper's link-set restore at its start, `LinkSet::restore` in `src/run/links.rs`, one pass from offset 0) takes each line through `Read::take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`, its `\n` counted, and counts what it steps over, per read (`Skipped{unknown_kinds, unknown_fields, torn_lines}`, not logged): an over-long line, a line that is not one JSON object and an unterminated last line are `torn_lines`; a line of a kind this build does not know is `unknown_kinds` and is not returned; a known-kind line with a key outside its contract is returned and counted once as `unknown_fields`. `link` and `unlink` are kinds this build knows since chunk 2026-10-10-session-links, so the reader returns such a line and no longer counts it under `unknown_kinds`. A reader never writes. The link-set restore runs beside the wait feed's rebuild and before the endpoint serves, so a start reads the log twice (`WaitFeed::rebuild`, then `LinkSet::restore`); the restore appends nothing and logs nothing. It takes each returned line through the link rule `viola_state::replay::apply_link_line`, which uses a `link` / `unlink` line's `data.driver` and `data.driven` only when both are strings, does not parse them as names again (the wrapper wrote them: the driver from a `from` or from a served `link` / `unlink` method's `params.driver`, each having passed `ViolaName::try_new`, the driven its own name), and changes nothing on a line of another kind or with a name that is no string.
 The next append heals a torn last line: under the lock every append holds, after a one-byte read of the log's end, it writes one LF ahead of its line in the same single write and logs one `state-recovered` line (a detail code, the file's basename and an offset, no content). The classified snapshot read (`viola_state::snapshot::read_snapshot_classified`) and the log replay (`viola_state::replay`) read through the same bounds and write no file.   - `viola-state`: home 0700/0600 creation (the pinned `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola` is the only 0700 file) and the Unix strict-modes check, including the trusted files and the `mode & 0o077` read rule on the home and `instances/<name>/`; on Windows, the protected user + SYSTEM DACL for a `--home` outside `%USERPROFILE%` and the owner + DACL startup check (windows-sys).
  - `viola-state`: SHA-256 re-hash of `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola(.exe)` before reuse. The hash crate is `sha2 =0.11.0` (Decisions Log `2026-09-25`).
  - `viola run` / `viola-state`: rewrite `plugin/<version>-<hash>/` files and `instances/<name>/settings.json` with the shared tempfile `persist` helper (0600, mode set on the temp file before the write) at every start, never reusing an existing copy. The `settings.json` override is rewritten on Unix when the pinned path passes the plain-character rule; it is not written on Windows or for a pinned path a shell could misread (§ Data Protection, Code-bearing artefacts). Every exec-form `command` they carry is the absolute pinned `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola(.exe)` path, never a PATH lookup (§ Universal). `ledger/stamps.json` is written only by `viola verify`, under its `.lock`, with 0600.

subject: errors
text: - `hook` never writes to stderr and never exits non-zero (Hook Contract). A security check failing in `hook` (server verification mismatch, oversized stdin, strict-modes failure) still ends in exit 0 with no body, so the dialog renders for the human. As landed, `viola hook <event>` runs the stdin cap, the `VIOLA_NAME` / `VIOLA_DIR` shape checks and the one-object parse and, on Linux and Windows, the server verification (macOS the recorded gap), and fails open with `hook-decision` detail `oversize-stdin` · `malformed-json` · `channel-unreachable` · `server-verify-failed`; strict-modes is owed to "Home and code-bearing file integrity" (Decisions Log `2026-09-28`). Its hidden `--capture <DIR>` arm runs the stdin cap, the absolute, existing `<DIR>` check and the exclusive `create_private_new` claim, and writes the capture raw; with `--answers <DIR>` it also runs the `take(64)` closed-`ProbeAnswer` read and `probe_body`'s payload shape check, and prints one `decision_body` body to stdout only for a mapped answer. Its statusline form `hook statusline --capture <DIR> [--shell <WORD>]` runs the same stdin cap and `<DIR>` check and claim, writes the payload raw and the closed shell verdict, and prints nothing on any path. On every failure it prints nothing, its stderr is always empty, and it exits 0 (Decisions Log `2026-09-28`, capture arm; the founder's live ruling of 2026-10-05 on `--answers`; the founder's own answer to P4 fork 3 of chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows («Run B + --settings», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I1`), on the statusline form).

text:
- NEVER write any channel frame (`send`, `answer`, `hook.dialog`, `wait`/`last`, `pause`/`release`, `link`/`unlink`, and `hook.event` notifications, which carry prompt and reply text) before verifying the server's pid (Windows: the connected stream's peer pid, interprocess `peer_creds().pid()`, which calls `GetNamedPipeServerProcessId` on the SQOS-adopted client end) or euid + pid (Linux/FreeBSD `peer_creds()`; the client-side euid check owed to the route entry "Unix endpoint and home hardening") plus sysinfo start time against `snapshot.json` (on macOS, where `peer_creds()` gives no pid: euid + the verified 0700 socket directory only, per the recorded known gap; the euid check is never skipped), and NEVER take those reference values (`endpoint`, `pid`, `started_at`) from a `snapshot.json` that has not passed the strict-modes check in the same process. The dated exceptions hold only the strict-modes half — the reference values taken from a `snapshot.json` read without the strict-modes check — owed to the Epoch 6 entry "Home and code-bearing file integrity"; on Linux and Windows each frame below verifies the serving process first (macOS: the recorded gap): `viola hook`'s `hook.event` (Decisions Log `2026-09-28`, ratified by the founder), CLI `viola send`'s `send` frame, CLI `viola wait` / `viola last`'s `wait` / `last` frames and CLI `viola answer`'s `answer` frame and CLI `viola pause` / `viola release`'s `pause` / `release` frames, each after the liveness pre-check and the server check, and `viola hook pre-tool-use|permission-request`'s `hook.dialog` frame after its payload shape check (the founder's rulings, live, 2026-10-04, relayed by the overseer; `answer` / `hook.dialog` the sixth dated gap; `pause` / `release` the seventh, F-W1), and `viola mcp`'s `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` tool frames after the liveness pre-check and the server check (the eighth dated gap: the founder's own answer to P4 fork Q1, 2026-10-17, relayed by the overseer, `inputs#I2` of chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers); no other frame or process may borrow any of them.
 CLI `viola link` / `viola unlink`'s `link` / `unlink` frames meet this ban in full: they take `endpoint`, `pid` and `started_at` from a `snapshot.json` read after `check_instance` passed in the same process and verify the server through `cmd::client::connect` on Linux and Windows; only every client's euid check and macOS's pid and start-time check stay owed to "Unix endpoint and home hardening", and they borrow no dated exception.

origin: ## Security Anti-Patterns (NEVER do these) › ### Code Patterns
text: - NEVER let a test-side removal under `target/e2e-home` take anything but a dir the test side itself created: the root fixture chain's owner sweep and a test home's drop (by `owner.json` record, by its own `TempDir`) and harness `cleanup` (by the `viola-session-` name). On the Linux dev host that path is a link to the per-user tmpfs directory `/tmp/viola-e2e-home-<uid>`, so these creations and removals reach outside the working directory: a boundary widening, ratified by the founder (live, 2026-10-07T07:25Z, after it was shown to him as creating and deleting outside the working directory through the link; relayed by the overseer). The two keepers (`prepare_home_base` in `tests/support/home.rs`, `Workspace::ensure_e2e_home` in the harness) NEVER follow a linked base unless its target is absolute and one `lstat` of it reads a real directory with no group or other bit; a target that is itself a link is refused, so is a backing whose filesystem reads less than the 9 GiB headroom floor free (`statvfs`), and a refusal is a fixed message that names no path (the headroom one holds the two counts). They create the target with mode 0700 through the directory builder (never a chmod after, never a parent) and remove nothing. Ownership is not read separately: the `tempdir_in` that follows succeeds in an owner-only directory only for its owner. `viola` itself never reads or writes the backing by that name, and no CI runner has the link.
